final_message:
I've filled in the Week One Test Plan and saved it as **Completed Week One Test Plan**. I haven't emailed it to the plant manager; that's still for you to do. I checked every total against the rules on the Test Rules tab and found no conflicts.

**The plan**
- **Who runs it:** the two most senior operators and water spiders who aren't on discipline. TM13 and TM18 were skipped because they are on discipline.

| Press | Operator | Water Spider | Tooling packs | Day 1 | Day 2 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TM19 | TM20 | T1/0, T3/0, T12 | 408 min | 180 min | 588 min (9.80 hrs) |
| 2 | TM17 | TM16 | T6, T8, T14, T16 | 365 min | 300 min | 665 min (11.08 hrs) |

- **Rules:** every day is under 450 minutes, each person is well under 2,250 minutes for the week, and Press 1 has 3 changeovers and Press 2 has 4.
- **Days needed:** all 56 packs are done in two days, so Days 3–5 are blank.
- **Tooling:** there is only one of each tooling pack, so each pack stays on one press and all its parts run back to back. That keeps changeovers to the minimum.
- **Time per part:** press minutes are packs × pack yards ÷ yards per hour × 60. In the plan sheet, each tooling pack's changeover-in minutes are on its first part and the changeover-out minutes on its last.
- **Material:**
  - **Polymer:** 280 lb each of ABS and TPO, and 140 lb each of PVC, TPE, TPU and TPV.
  - **Wire:** 200 yards each of G16, G14 and G12, 160 yards each of G8 and G6, and 120 yards each of G1/0 and G3/0.

**Decision for you:** the BOM footnote says 50 lb of polymer per unit, but the BOM table says 20 lb for every part. I used the table's 20 lb. If 50 lb is right, every polymer amount goes up 2.5 times (ABS would be 700 lb, for example). Please get Engineering or Quality to confirm before material is issued.

**Other assumptions**, all stated on a "Plan Notes & Assumptions" tab I added to the file:
- The "Labor Minutes" column is press run time per part. Each of the two crew members on that press works those minutes, so total crew labor is double: 2,506 minutes, about 41.8 hours.
- Each person's total includes changeover time, on the assumption that the press crew does or attends the changeovers.
- No allowance is planned for scrap, sample parts, or cleaning out polymer between parts on the same tooling, because none of these is given in the reference files.

The notes tab also shows how many full packages of each material need to be issued and what will be left over.

DONE
